reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a no-code flashloan arbitrage bot and directs viewers to deposit through MetaMask and stake in FlashBot pools. It links minimum deposits of 0.3 ETH or 1 BNB to claims of automated arbitrage profits, more than 11 ETH from one trade, a 10% airdrop, and displayed 200 ETH and 1000 BNB airdrop promotions.

When you have selected your loan amount, click on the deposit button. Confirm the MetaMask transaction
I made more than 11 Ether with this one trade I made
The first part is to stake in one of the FlashBot pools

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker explicitly warns that many flashloan videos are scams or no longer work and says they tested other platforms before describing this one. That gives the presentation a testing-and-warning dimension, not just an earnings pitch. The speaker also identifies gas fees and the possibility of being front-run, so the account does not portray every trade as costless or risk-free. Those cautions do not prove the platform works, but they matter when deciding whether the video is simply a deceptive solicitation.

Ether or BNB to cover the gas fees
because of the risk of getting front run by other arbitrage flash loans

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited claim of making more than 11 Ether is framed as one trade the speaker says they made, not an explicit promise that every viewer will make the same amount. Likewise, a deposit instruction shows a transaction step, but does not by itself establish what ultimately happens to a viewer's funds. The warning about scam videos and failed platforms is context the opening leaves out.

When you have selected your loan amount, click on the deposit button. Confirm the MetaMask transaction.
Though beware, most videos on YouTube are actually scams,. Or no longer work.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warning is immediately followed by the speaker's claim that this is the only bot that worked for them; it functions as a reason to trust the promoted platform, not as an investigation of it. Mentioning costs and front-running does not temper the instruction to confirm a deposit or the claim of a large return from one trade. The pool pitch goes further by promising profits on autopilot.

opening.argument: Judge, much of the video walks through an operational sequence: choosing a token tracker, copying a contract address and ticker, entering them into the tool, and starting an arbitrage search. The speaker describes using Uniswap token as an example and later demonstrates pool and withdrawal controls. Earnings claims accompany that walkthrough, but a tutorial showing what a tool purports to do is not itself proof that the presenter has misrepresented its operation. Read the first-person result as part of a demonstration, not as a verified outcome for future users.

citations.quote: Now you'll be taken to the official Token Tracker page, where you can find the contract address for the token you want to make an arbitrage trade on.
I'm going to use Uniswap token as an example. Now you copy the token address, and remember its ticker.
Paste the token address into the address box, and then type the ticker into the token symbol text box. Then click on the Start Arbitrage Finder button.
To withdraw from the pool, just go back to the pools page. Click on withdraw, and sign the transaction

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening accurately identifies deposit and staking steps, but those steps appear inside a longer walkthrough that starts with selecting a token and entering its contract address. Nor does the speaker's claim about one profitable trade verify that the trade occurred or establish that viewers are guaranteed the same result. The record supports calling this an instructional promotion; the cited steps alone do not settle whether the underlying tool is fraudulent.

citations.quote: Now you copy the token address, and remember its ticker.
When you have selected your loan amount, click on the deposit button. Confirm the MetaMask transaction.
I made more than 11 Ether with this one trade I made.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial framing does not make the money-making instructions incidental. After the token-entry steps, the speaker directs viewers to deposit and confirm a wallet transaction, then claims they will receive profit. The pool walkthrough similarly asks viewers to stake funds for purported automated profits. Showing controls and narrating a result does not substantiate either the claimed trade return or the safety of following those instructions.

Now the platform has executed the arbitrage trade and paid back the flash. Loan you will receive the profit on your wallet.
The first part is to stake in one of the FlashBot pools, not only will you get the airdrop,. But you will also generate profits from FlashLoan arbitrage on autopilot.

opening.argument: Judge, this can be read as promotion of a no-code service with a stated workflow, not evidence of a demonstrated theft mechanism. The speaker describes selecting an amount, approving a MetaMask transaction, executing a trade and using a withdrawal control. The account does not show a request for a seed phrase or a referral downline, and its claim about receiving profit is not the same as evidence that funds were taken. None of that establishes the service is safe; it does limit what can be concluded from the presentation alone.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies substantial advertised returns and a minimum pool deposit, but it does not show that the deposit was stolen or that withdrawal failed. Indeed, the speaker describes a withdrawal path. The claimed trade result and airdrop may warrant skepticism; treating them as verified fraud goes beyond what these sources establish about actual transactions.

citations.quote: the minimum deposit is 0.3 ether or 1 BNB
To withdraw from the pool, just go back to the pools page. Click on withdraw, and sign the transaction, you will get your stake as well as the profits.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A failed withdrawal or seed-phrase request is not necessary to recognize the pitch. The speaker instructs viewers to deposit through a wallet, says a trade produced more than 11 Ether, and ties pool staking to automated profits and a 10% airdrop. A narrated withdrawal option does not verify that viewers can recover funds. The material promotes sending funds in pursuit of extraordinary claimed returns, regardless of whether an eventual loss is documented.
